spec_match.rationale: Calls the exact surfaces the WebIDL names (Proofreader.availability()/create() with expectedInputLanguages, proofread()), but the banner's flag guidance (chrome://flags/#proofreader-api) looks inexact and the behind-a-flag/origin-trial framing is stale now that Proofreader is exposed by default in Chromium 141 (observed in this session's browser).

interactive.rationale: Editable textarea plus Probe API and Proofread buttons drive a real availability() probe and a real proofread() call, with a clearly-labelled client-side stub fallback whose status line always names which path ran.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index blurb promises an on-device grammar/spelling probe against Chrome's model family, and that is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Unavailable API, availability() states, and create/proofread failures are handled, but there is no downloadprogress/monitor handling, no AbortSignal use, and no includeCorrectionTypes or non-English coverage; the stub only recognises eight canned patterns.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5164677291835392 (verified correct id) and the feature page.

conformance.rationale: A suite exists but its script assertions are tolerant both ways (e.g. typeof Proofreader==='undefined'||typeof Proofreader==='function'), so they can never fail and prove neither presence nor contract — flagged for a human; existing assertions were not touched.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI: desktop 1280px and mobile 360px screenshots, DOM dump, zero console errors (one fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet failure is environmental); buttons could not be clicked in this environment so the probe/proofread flows were verified by code trace only.

telemetry_health.rationale: The injected demo-telemetry script captures global errors, but the page records no per-interaction asserts for probe outcome or real-vs-stub proofread path.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables and correct button colour overrides throughout, but small-text status colours miss WCAG AA: .status.ok emerald #0a8f5c on ivory ≈4.05:1 and .status.warn amber ≈3.5:1, and .corr ivory-on-emerald chips ≈4.05:1.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled textarea and native buttons are keyboard-operable with visible focus, but the status line and corrections output are not live regions, so async results arrive silently for screen-reader users.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: responsive-support.json records this feature untested on both classes; the single-column layout showed no desktop overflow, and the 360px CLI capture is inconclusive because this headless build clamps window width below 500px (layout cropped, not page overflow), so genuine mobile evidence is missing.

openQuestions.title: Refresh the flag banner with the exact flag id and Chrome 141+ default availability
openQuestions.detail: The banner names chrome://flags/#proofreader-api, but the Chromium flag for this API family is believed to be #proofreader-api-for-gemini-nano (verify in runtime_enabled_features.json5 / chrome://flags before editing). More importantly, window.Proofreader is exposed by default in Chromium 141 (observed in this session's headless 141 run where the conformance route exercised the global), so 'Behind a flag ... or join the origin trial' is stale for current visitors. Keep the v139 origin-trial history but state present-day availability.

openQuestions.title: Flag for human: proofreader conformance assertions cannot fail
openQuestions.detail: Five of six assertions in v139/proofreader-api/conformance.json are of the form typeof X==='undefined'||<check>, which passes whether the API exists or not — the probe-can't-return-false anti-pattern. Existing assertions are immutable and were not edited; a human should decide whether to supersede the suite with strict presence assertions now that the API ships by default.

openQuestions.title: Add aria-live to status/output and per-interaction telemetry asserts
openQuestions.detail: Give #status role=status (aria-live=polite) and make #out a live region so probe and proofread results are announced; add showcaseTelemetry.assert calls distinguishing real-API vs stub runs so production telemetry can see which path visitors hit.

openQuestions.title: Run the responsive matrix for v139/proofreader-api
openQuestions.detail: The feature is still 'untested/seed' in responsive-support.json. Run `deno task responsive-check v139/proofreader-api --merge` with a real 360x740 emulated viewport (this session's CLI headless clamps window width, so its mobile capture is not valid evidence).

summary: The probe exercises the real Proofreader surface with an honestly-labelled stub fallback and correct references, but its flag/origin-trial banner has gone stale (the API is default-enabled in Chromium 141), the conformance suite is vacuously green, statuses miss AA contrast by a small margin, and there is no live-region or assert coverage. Verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshots, DOM dump, clean console); interactive controls could not be driven in this environment, so runtime evidence is partial.
